title: Customer escalation war-room prep: NYC pilot outage
content:
Goal: Rapidly triage and neutralize ongoing latency/failed-response issue affecting NYC pilot customer (Acme MQ). Prep notes for 1st war-room (standup + roles, ~30-45m).

Background:
- Start time: 2026-02-25 22:40 UTC (first alerts).
- Symptom: ~25% of requests to model 'redwood-2b-quant' returning error 503 or timing out >10s. Intermittent but sustained for ~3 hours.
- Scope: NYC pilot environment (dedicated pool). Estimated % of customer traffic impacted: 60% peak.
- Business impact: customer-facing latency spikes, retries causing higher cost and downstream failures for their ingestion pipeline. Legal/contract: pilot, but high risk of churn.
- Current status: infra team identified increased GPU mem pressure on pool; rolling restart scheduled for 2026-02-26 01:00 UTC. No rollback yet.

Attendees (invite list):
- Alex Kim (owner, CS lead)
- Priya Nair (customer engineering lead)
- Luis Gonzalez (platform eng on-call)
- Heather Park (SRE)
- Mark Lee (customer PM, Acme MQ) - optional
- Ops on-call (TBD)

War-room agenda (30m):
1) Quick context and impact summary (3m) - Alex
2) Live telemetry snapshot (5m) - Heather/Luis (latency distribution, 503s, GPU mem metrics)
3) Customer-facing comms status + draft (5m) - Priya/Alex
4) Immediate mitigations and responsibilities (10m) - decide actions (restart/scale/route)
5) Post-mortem owners, next check-in time, and action list (5m)

Telemetry checklist (what to pull before/at start):
- Query Datadog dashboards: per-route latency, 503 rate, retry rates (last 6h, 1h)
- GPU utilization and memory fragmentation on dedicated pool nodes (last 3h)
- Model runtime logs: OOM traces, kernel failures, queue backlog metrics
- Routing logs: which routes were pinned to pool/region
- Customer logs: timestamps of failed requests, request payload samples (sanitized)

Draft customer message (short):
Subject: Brief outage update - Redwood inference latency for NYC pilot
Hi Mark / Acme team,
We're actively investigating increased latency and intermittent 503 responses you've been seeing. We've assembled a response team and will share updates every 30 minutes until resolved. Current estimated ETA for mitigation steps: ~1-2 hours. Apologies for the disruption - prioritizing a stable rollout path.
(Will send first update at 23:00 UTC)

Immediate mitigation options (pros/cons):
- Rolling restart of affected pool nodes (Heather)
  - Pros: clears memory fragmentation, quick.
  - Cons: temporary reduced capacity, potential transient errors during restart.
- Route traffic to cold standby pool (if capacity available) (Luis)
  - Pros: minimal risk to customers during switch.
  - Cons: requires config change + verification; standby may not be sized for peak.
- Fallback to smaller model variant (redwood-1b) for high-latency routes (Priya)
  - Pros: lowers mem pressure, quick config change via routing rules.
  - Cons: potential quality degradation for customer prompts.
- Increase autoscale burst to add nodes (platform)
  - Pros: addresses capacity short-term.
  - Cons: may take several minutes, depends on quota and available infra.

Proposed immediate plan (consensus suggestion):
1) Execute rolling restart of 3 most affected nodes staggered by 2 min to limit impact (owner: Heather).
2) In parallel, prepare routing to standby pool (owner: Luis) - ready but do not switch unless errors persist after restarts.
3) Prepare safe fallback routing to redwood-1b for non-critical routes (owner: Priya) - only toggle if error rate not improved in 15m after restarts.
4) Send first customer update by 23:00 UTC (owner: Alex/Priya).

Action items (post-war-room to track):
- Heather: Start rolling restart at 2026-02-26 01:00 UTC; post status at each node restart completion. Due: 2026-02-26 02:00 UTC.
- Luis: Confirm standby pool health & pre-warm if needed; prepare routing playbook (how to switch back). Due: 2026-02-26 00:45 UTC.
- Priya: Draft and send customer comms; prepare fallback route config for redwood-1b. Due: 2026-02-25 23:00 UTC (first comms); fallback config by 2026-02-26 00:15 UTC.
- Alex: Coordinate updates, own next 30m check-in, escalate to director if >2h outage. Due: ongoing (next check-in 2026-02-26 00:30 UTC).
- SRE team (ops): Capture logs and preserve affected node images for post-mortem. Due: before restart.

Notes to self / rough checklist:
- Bring up the incident doc in Confluence and attach JIRA-INC-4321 (done).
- Ensure Slack #cs-nyc-incident pinned messages include customer contact + escalation matrix.
- Remind customer PM that change windows will cause brief additional retries; ask for tolerance.
- Check cost implications and quota for autoscale burst (Finance note later).

Follow-ups / Post-mortem agenda (if incident >1h or service-affecting):
- Timeline reconstruction (MVP single source of truth) - owner: Heather
- Root cause analysis: mem fragmentation vs regression vs model binary issue - owner: Luis
- Customer impact analysis + credits/compensation recommendation - owner: Alex/Priya
- Action plan for preventing recurrence (kernel fixes, autoscale tuning, routing fallback automation) - owners: platform + runtime teams

Unresolved questions to raise in war-room:
- Is there a known regression deployed to pool in last 24h? (link PRs)
- Any scheduled maintenance or jobs that increase memory load?
- Are we seeing any correlated errors in other regions/pools?

Quick bookmarks (links to fetch at start):
- Datadog: /d/redwood/nyc-pilot-latency (dashboard)
- Grafana: GPU pool memory heatmap
- JIRA: JIRA-INC-4321
- Confluence incident doc: confluence/redwood/nyc-pilot-incident

End notes: keep war-room tight, aim for 30m decision cycle, owners write short next-steps in the doc, avoid long theory discussion in first call.

-- Alex

(Version: draft v0.3 - will update after 1st war-room)
